title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in June 2026: Defect passivation, composition and phase control
abstract: From a monthly corpus of 623 indexed publications in perovskite photovoltaics, critical examination of 167 works reveals that unstandardized characterization continues to conflate reversible ionic polarization with enduring chemical defect remediation. Only 14 studies report independently certified performance metrics, establishing a verified efficiency boundary of 33.6% for tandem configurations and 27.28% for single-junction devices. These certified frontiers rely on multidentate Lewis-base chelators that elevate vacancy formation energies, dense self-assembled monolayer (SAM) hole contacts that suppress interfacial deprotonation, and interfacial strain relief that impedes nucleation of hexagonal non-perovskite phases. However, severe geometric scaling penalties persist across larger formats, reducing certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) to 26.8% at an aperture area of \qty{655.2}{\centi\meter}$^2$ as macroscopic contact pinholes, sheet resistance, and solvent washouts induce non-radiative recombination. Standardized operational stability evidence remains thin: merely 6 investigations document operational lifetime thresholds, with the longest duration reaching \qty{3600}{\hour}, and only 3 adhere to International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) testing procedures. A pervasive reporting disparity accentuates this ambiguity, as 48.1% of publications declare efficiency values while only 5.9% provide independent certification, leaving uncertified claims vulnerable to sweep-rate hysteresis, aperture misalignment, and capacitive transients. Mechanistically, evidence confirms that multidentate coordination and steric hindrance mitigate lead vacancy formation and fullerene photo-dimerization, while catalytic anchoring protects selective contacts against solvent erosion. Nevertheless, macroscopic work-function shifts routinely conceal severe nanoscale contact disorder and trapped-hole accumulation. Bulk structural probes fail to distinguish thermodynamic phase stabilization from kinetically trapped metastable states, and macroscopic measurements conceal substantial morphological disparities across sequentially deposited scaffolds. Because current lifetime testing lacks uniform electrical bias and thermal baselines, available data cannot verify whether contact reconstruction confers greater operational longevity than molecular passivation, necessitating operando impedance spectroscopy and drive-level capacitance profiling under continuous stress.
